audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL transaction processing (gas economics, EVM memory, calldata pricing, EOF bytecode validation, contract creation), CL validator duties (sync committees, block proposals with execution payloads), and their interfaces (Engine API). Both EL and CL are materially present.

out_of_scope: Execution Layer internals when viewed from CL perspective

el_attack_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions, calldata spam attacks exploiting reduced gas costs (EIP-2028), oversized blob transactions (EIP-7594), malicious EOF bytecode deployment (EIP-7692)
Eclipse attacks, send false transaction announcements with spoofed metadata (EIP-8077), provide invalid column samples (EIP-7594), send invalid blocks

cl_attack_vectors.threat: Submit false sync committee messages, propose blocks with invalid execution payloads, manipulate aggregation
Provide incorrect execution payloads, manipulate fee recipients, denial of service on Engine API

misclassified_entities.reason: Internal EL component - the EVM interpreter is part of the execution layer under audit, not an external entity
Internal EVM execution context - smart contracts executing within the EVM are internal to the EL
Internal EVM bytecode execution - contract code runs within the EVM, which is an internal EL component
Internal EVM opcode implementation - opcode callers are internal to the EVM execution engine
Internal CL component - the beacon chain is the CL itself, which is in scope as a target component, not an external entity
Internal CL component - the fork choice store is part of the consensus layer under audit
Local operator configuration - not an external entity sending data into the system over a network boundary; it is local trusted configuration
Historical PoW chain is an internal precursor state of the EL, not an active external entity sending data into the current system

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via devp2p
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes communicate over unauthenticated P2P network. Any peer can send false transaction announcements with spoofed sender addresses and nonces (EIP-8077), invalid blocks, or malicious data. No authentication required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users and DApps submit transactions via public JSON-RPC. No authentication required. Transactions may contain malicious calldata, oversized blobs, or malformed EOF bytecode. Covers EIP-2028 calldata, EIP-7594 blob transactions, and EIP-7692 EOF contract deployments.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Column Custodian via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes that custody columns respond to DAS sampling requests over unauthenticated P2P. They may withhold data, provide invalid column proofs, or manipulate node ID assignment to concentrate custody.

trusted_external_entities.name: Sync Committee Subnet Peer via gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators on sync committee subnets publish messages over P2P gossip. Peers may submit false sync committee messages, attempt to manipulate aggregation, or delay messages to degrade light client security.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer / Miner via P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P block propagation, block header validation
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block producers broadcast blocks over P2P network. They may create blocks with maximally-sized calldata to slow propagation (EIP-2028 concern), propose blocks with invalid PoW (EIP-1588), or include invalid transactions.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Deployer via JSON-RPC / Transaction
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Contract creation transactions (CREATE, EOFCREATE, initcode transactions)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Deployers submit contract creation transactions. EOF containers (EIP-7692) must be fully validated at deploy time. Malicious deployers may craft bytecode attempting to bypass validation, exploit stack analysis, or trigger edge cases in CALLF/RETF/JUMPF handling.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The CL communicates with the EL via JWT-authenticated Engine API. The channel is authenticated, but payload content (execution payloads, fork choice state) must still be validated by the EL. A compromised CL client could send invalid payloads.

trusted_external_entities.name: Execution Engine via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Engine API responses (payload_id, execution payload, SYNCING status)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The EL execution engine provides execution payloads to the CL validator via JWT-authenticated Engine API. The channel is authenticated, but a compromised execution engine could return invalid payloads, causing the validator to propose invalid blocks (Bellatrix). Content validation required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via CL Gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: CL peers propagate blocks and attestations over unauthenticated P2P gossip. Peers may send invalid blocks, conflicting attestations, or attempt eclipse attacks. All received data must be fully validated.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Announced metadata (hash, type, size, address, nonce) is UNVERIFIED and must only be used as optimization hints, never for security decisions. Full transaction must be retrieved and independently validated. Protocol violations (metadata mismatch) must result in peer penalization.

Blocks received from peers must be fully validated (header, PoW/PoS, state transitions, gas limits). Block size may be larger due to cheaper calldata (EIP-2028); propagation delays must not exceed security bounds.

Full transaction validation required: intrinsic gas check (EIP-2028 calldata pricing), blob count limits (max 6 per EIP-7594), cell proof verification (KZG batch verify), versioned hash matching. Reject transactions failing any check.

All received column samples must have KZG proofs batch-verified against known commitments. Insufficient valid samples indicate data withholding. Node ID manipulation for custody concentration must be mitigated. Reconstruction requires >=50% of columns.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Sync committee gossip subnet message handler
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Sync committee messages must be signature-verified. Aggregators must verify beacon_block_root consistency. Best contribution selection must use highest signature count. Clock synchronization assumed for 1/3 and 2/3 slot timing deadlines.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Block validation pipeline (header, PoW, state transition)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Blocks must be validated against the correct consensus ruleset based on block number (e.g., EIP-1588 fork boundary at 7280000). PoW verification must use the appropriate algorithm. Blocks with excessive calldata must not degrade network propagation below security bounds.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Contract creation handler (CREATE, EOFCREATE, initcode transactions)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: EOF containers must pass full structural validation (magic bytes, header, sections), code validation (valid opcodes, EIP-3670), static stack analysis (no underflow/overflow, EIP-5450), and function call validation (CALLF/RETF/JUMPF, EIP-4750/6206). Both initcode and deployed code must be validated. Invalid containers must be rejected at deploy time.

JWT authentication verifies channel identity. Execution payloads received via newPayload must be independently validated by the EL (state transition, gas limits, transaction validity). Fork choice updates must be validated against EL's view of the chain. SYNCING status must be handled gracefully.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Engine API responses (engine_getPayload response, payload status)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: JWT authentication verifies channel identity. Execution payloads returned by the EL must be structurally valid. The CL validator must verify payload fits within beacon block constraints. If execution engine returns SYNCING or error, the validator should skip block proposal for safety.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Beacon block gossip handler, attestation gossip handler
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All received beacon blocks must pass beacon state transition validation AND execution payload validation (via Engine API). Attestations must be signature-verified. Invalid blocks/attestations must be rejected. Peers sending invalid data should be penalized.
